title: Verbs that end in -s
title_target: Det var länge sedan vi sågs!
goal: Use the verbs that always end in *-s* (*hoppas, finnas, minnas, låtsas, andas, trivas*) and the *-s* that means "each other" (*vi ses, vi träffas, vi hörs, kramas*).
bekal: deponent verbs: an *-s* ending with an ordinary active meaning
reciprocal verbs: *Vi ses! Vi hörs! Ska vi träffas?*
the forms: *minns – mindes – mints*, *finns – fanns – funnits*
wave: Go back to Unit 3: say the ten particle verbs aloud with the stress on the particle, then use five of them with inte in a main clause — Jag tycker inte om…, Han kommer aldrig ihåg…

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Återseendet
dialogs.intro: A month after the move, Dian runs into Ahmad, her old corridor neighbor from Lappis, outside a café on Götgatan. They haven't seen each other since moving day.

lines.speaker: Ahmad:
lines.text: Dian! Det var länge sedan vi sågs!
lines.id: Dian! It's been ages since we saw each other!
lines.literal: Dian! it was long since we saw-each-other!

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ahmad! Kom hit, vi måste kramas! Hur mår du?
lines.id: Ahmad! Come here, we have to hug! How are you?
lines.literal: Ahmad! come here, we must hug-each-other! how feel you?

lines.speaker: Ahmad:
lines.text: Bra, tack. Jag trivs fortfarande i korridoren, men det är tyst utan dig.
lines.id: Good, thanks. I still like it in the corridor, but it's quiet without you.
lines.literal: good, thanks. I thrive still in corridor-the, but it is quiet without you.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Minns du när brandlarmet gick klockan tre på natten?
lines.id: Do you remember when the fire alarm went off at three in the morning?
lines.literal: remember you when fire-alarm-the went clock-the three on night-the?

lines.speaker: Ahmad:
lines.text: Klart jag minns! Alla stod ute i snön och låtsades att de inte frös.
lines.id: Of course I remember! Everybody stood outside in the snow pretending they weren't cold.
lines.literal: of-course I remember! all stood outside in snow-the and pretended that they not froze.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Och du sa: "Andas lugnt, det är bara Oskars popcorn."
lines.id: And you said, "Breathe calmly, it's just Oskar's popcorn."
lines.literal: and you said: breathe calmly, it is only Oskar's popcorn.

lines.speaker: Ahmad:
lines.text: Och det var det också! Hur är det i kollektivet?
lines.id: And that's exactly what it was! How's life in the shared flat?
lines.literal: and it was that also! how is it in collective-the?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Underbart. Det finns alltid någon att prata med. Men jag saknar våra middagar.
lines.id: Wonderful. There's always someone to talk to. But I miss our dinners.
lines.literal: wonderful. it exists always someone to talk with. but I miss our dinners.

lines.speaker: Ahmad:
lines.text: Vi kan träffas på fredagar, om du vill.
lines.id: We could meet up on Fridays, if you like.
lines.literal: we can meet-each-other on Fridays, if you want.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Gärna! Fast nästa vecka börjar jag en kvällskurs i svenska. Läraren heter Lena.
lines.id: I'd love to! Although next week I'm starting an evening class in Swedish. The teacher's called Lena.
lines.literal: gladly! though next week start I an evening-course in Swedish. teacher-the is-called Lena.

lines.speaker: Ahmad:
lines.text: Lena Berg? Hon var min lärare också. Hon är fantastisk.
lines.id: Lena Berg? She was my teacher too. She's fantastic.
lines.literal: Lena Berg? she was my teacher also. she is fantastic.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Vad bra. Jag hoppas att hon inte märker hur nervös jag är.
lines.id: That's good. I hope she doesn't notice how nervous I am.
lines.literal: how good. I hope that she not notices how nervous I am.

lines.speaker: Ahmad:
lines.text: Ingen fara. Hon säger alltid: "Det finns inga dumma frågor."
lines.id: Don't worry. She always says, "There are no stupid questions."
lines.literal: no danger. she says always: it exists no stupid questions.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det låter bra. Nu måste jag gå, men vi hörs, okej?
lines.id: That sounds good. I have to go now, but let's talk soon, okay?
lines.literal: that sounds good. now must I go, but we hear-each-other, okay?

lines.speaker: Ahmad:
lines.text: Vi hörs! Och vi ses på fredag.
lines.id: Talk soon! And see you on Friday.
lines.literal: we hear-each-other! and we see-each-other on Friday.

notes: **Vi sågs, vi ses** — the *-s* on the end of *se* turns "see" into "see **each other**". *Vi ses* (**vi SEHS**) is the everyday Swedish "See you!" and *Det var länge sedan vi sågs* (**SOHGS**) is "It's been ages since we saw each other." One little letter does the work of two English words.

**Vi måste kramas** — *kramas* means "hug each other". **En kram** is a hug, and Swedes hug friends hello and goodbye far more than their reserved reputation suggests. *Kram!* or *Kramar!* at the end of a text message is the equivalent of "Hugs!" or "xx".

**Minns du…?** — *minnas* (**MIN-nahs**) means "remember", just like *komma ihåg* from Unit 3. *Minnas* leans toward memories (*Jag minns min första snö*), *komma ihåg* toward not forgetting (*Kom ihåg nyckeln!*). The forms are irregular: *minns – mindes – mints*.

**Låtsades att de inte frös** — *låtsas* (**LOT-sahs**) means "pretend". Notice the BIFF rule at work in the *att*-clause: *att de **inte** frös*. **Frös** is the past of *frysa*, which means both "freeze" and "be cold": *Jag fryser!* — I'm cold!
**Andas lugnt** — the command form of *andas* (breathe) is simply *andas*. Verbs that always end in *-s* keep it everywhere, even in commands: *Andas! Hoppas på det bästa!* (Hope for the best!)

**Jag trivs** and **det finns** are two of the most useful *-s* verbs. *Trivas* (**TREE-vahs**) means "to like it somewhere, to feel at home": *Jag trivs i Stockholm.* English needs a whole phrase for it. *Det finns* is "there is / there are" — the normal way to say something exists: *Det finns inga dumma frågor.*

grammars.title: Deponent verbs: -s with an active meaning
body: Some Swedish verbs only exist with an *-s* on the end, yet they mean something perfectly active: you hope, you breathe, you remember. Grammarians call them **deponent verbs**. Don't look for a version without *-s* — *hoppa* is a different verb altogether ("jump").
after: The present is easy: take the ordinary present form and swap its final *-r* (or *-er*) for *-s*. Group 1 verbs therefore look the same in the infinitive and the present: *jag hoppas, jag andas*. Other verbs lose their *-e-* too: *trivas → trivs*, *finnas → finns*.
In the past, *-s* is simply added to the normal past form: *hoppade → hoppades*, *trivde → trivdes*. In the supine, *-t* becomes *-ts*: *lyckats, trivts*.

grammars.title: Reciprocal verbs: -s = each other
body: Add *-s* to some ordinary verbs and they mean that two or more people do something **to each other**. The subject is always plural (*vi, ni, de*, or two names).
after: You can always use the full form with *varandra* (each other) instead: *Vi träffar varandra* = *Vi träffas*. The *-s* form is shorter and more common in speech.
The same *-s* ending has a third job — making the passive (*Kaffet serveras kl 8*). That's the next unit.

When to use it
rows: you'll be in touch by phone or text
warmer still; often to someone leaving

blocks.text: Swedes often stack two or three of these at the end of a conversation: *Hej då, vi hörs! Ha det bra!* — and on the phone, a goodbye can go back and forth several times (*Hej hej! — Hej! — Hej då!*). Don't hang up after the first one.

blocks.title: Signing off a message
items: **Med vänliga hälsningar** (often written **Mvh**) — Kind regards (formal emails)
*Det finns ingen mjölk kvar.* — There's no milk left.
*Fanns det något bröd?* — Was there any bread?
*Det syns att du är trött.* — You can tell you're tired. (literally: it shows)
*Trivs du på jobbet?* — Do you like it at work?

blocks.text: **Det finns** vs **det är**: use *det finns* when you say that something exists or is available — *Det finns en bra pizzeria här.* Use *det är* to identify or describe — *Det är en bra pizzeria.* English uses "there is" for the first and "it is" for the second, so the split is the same.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 1
items: Tell three short stories in the past with *-s* verbs and a time word: *I fredags sågs vi på Söder. I somras träffades vi i Göteborg. För två dagar sedan kramades vi på stationen.*
Then ask the questions: *När sågs ni senast? Var träffades ni?*
